subproblem.title: Continuous compactly supported maps are dense in L¹ of a finite measure on ℝ^N (Step 4 of the supplied proof)
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let E be a real normed space (E : Type with NormedAddCommGroup E and NormedSpace ℝ E), let ν be a finite measure on ℝ^N = Eucl N with its Borel σ-algebra (IsFiniteMeasure ν), and let f : ℝ^N → E belong to L¹(ν) (MemLp f 1 ν). Then for every ε ∈ [0, ∞] with ε ≠ 0 there is g : ℝ^N → E such that g has compact support (HasCompactSupport g), ‖f − g‖_{L¹(ν)} = eLpNorm (f − g) 1 ν ≤ ε, g is continuous and g ∈ L¹(ν) (MemLp g 1 ν).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (ν : Measure (Eucl N)) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (f : Eucl N → E), MemLp f 1 ν → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, ε ≠ 0 → ∃ g : Eucl N → E, HasCompactSupport g ∧ eLpNorm (f - g) 1 ν ≤ ε ∧ Continuous g ∧ MemLp g 1 ν
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4(b)–(c) of the supplied proof of imc_lintegral_coordNorm_le_mass (density of continuous compactly supported maps in L¹ of a finite Borel measure, proved from regularity and Urysohn's lemma), stated for a general coefficient space E. It is the case p = 1 of Mathlib's MemLp.exists_hasCompactSupport_eLpNorm_sub_le, whose file Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ContinuousMapDense.lean is not in the frozen import closure; the argument below reproduces that proof. The comparator-accepted proof of fiw_im_mass_formula (commit 83e1f61809c1, local `have hdense`) contains exactly this argument in Lean for ℝ^P; with P renamed to N it proves the present statement verbatim.

Notation. ‖h‖₁ := eLpNorm h 1 ν = ∫⁻ ‖h(x)‖ₑ dν(x) for h : ℝ^N → E. 1_s c denotes the function x ↦ c if x ∈ s and 0 otherwise (s.indicator fun _ => c). "Continuous compactly supported" means continuous with HasCompactSupport.

1. (Regularity and small indicators.) ν is a finite measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^N, a σ-compact (proper) metric space, so ν is outer regular and inner regular with respect to compact sets: (i) for every measurable s with ν(s) < ∞ and every η > 0 there is an open V ⊇ s with ν(V) < ∞ and ν(V ∖ s) < η (MeasurableSet.exists_isOpen_sdiff_lt); (ii) for every measurable t with ν(t) < ∞ and every η > 0 there is a compact (hence closed) s ⊆ t with ν(t ∖ s) < η (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_isClosed_sdiff_lt). Moreover (iii) for c ∈ E and δ ∈ (0, ∞] there is a real η > 0 such that ‖1_s c‖₁ ≤ δ for every null-measurable s with ν(s) ≤ η (exists_eLpNorm_indicator_le with p = 1; indeed ‖1_s c‖₁ = ‖c‖·ν(s)).

2. (Urysohn approximation of c·1_s.) Let s be closed, u open, s ⊆ u, ν(s) < ∞, c ∈ E and δ ≠ 0. Claim: there is a continuous h : ℝ^N → E with ‖h − 1_s c‖₁ ≤ δ, ‖h(x)‖ ≤ ‖c‖ for all x, support h ⊆ u, and h ∈ L¹(ν).
 - Take η for c and δ as in 1(iii), and by 1(i) an open V ⊇ s with ν(V) < ∞ and ν(V ∖ s) < η. Put v := u ∩ V; then s ⊆ v, v is open and ν(v) < ∞.
 - vᶜ and s are disjoint closed sets, so Urysohn's lemma (exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed) gives a continuous φ : ℝ^N → [0, 1] with φ = 0 on vᶜ and φ = 1 on s. Put h(x) := φ(x)·c.
 - h is continuous, ‖h(x)‖ = φ(x)‖c‖ ≤ ‖c‖, and h(x) = 0 off v, so support h ⊆ v ⊆ u. h ∈ L¹(ν): it is bounded by ‖c‖·1_v and ν(v) < ∞ (MemLp.smul of the L¹ function φ ≤ 1_v with the constant c).
 - Pointwise ‖h(x) − 1_s c(x)‖ ≤ ‖1_{v∖s} c(x)‖: on s both h and 1_s c equal c; on v ∖ s the left side is ‖h(x)‖ ≤ ‖c‖; off v both vanish. Hence ‖h − 1_s c‖₁ ≤ ‖1_{v∖s} c‖₁ ≤ δ by 1(iii), because v ∖ s is measurable and ν(v ∖ s) ≤ ν(V ∖ s) < η.

3. (Indicators of sets of finite measure.) Let t be measurable with ν(t) < ∞, c ∈ E and δ ≠ 0. Claim: there is g continuous, in L¹(ν), with compact support and ‖g − 1_t c‖₁ ≤ δ.
 - Choose δ' > 0 such that ‖a‖₁ ≤ δ' and ‖b‖₁ ≤ δ' imply ‖a + b‖₁ < δ (exists_Lp_half; for p = 1 any δ' with 2δ' < δ works by the triangle inequality).
 - Take η for c and δ' as in 1(iii), and by 1(ii) a compact closed s ⊆ t with ν(t ∖ s) < η. Then 1_s c − 1_t c = −1_{t∖s} c, so ‖1_s c − 1_t c‖₁ = ‖1_{t∖s} c‖₁ ≤ δ'.
 - ℝ^N is locally compact, so there is a compact k with s ⊆ interior k (exists_compact_superset). Apply Step 2 to s, u := interior k (open), c and δ' (ν(s) ≤ ν(t) < ∞): a continuous h ∈ L¹(ν) with support h ⊆ interior k and ‖h − 1_s c‖₁ ≤ δ'.
 - h − 1_t c = (h − 1_s c) + (1_s c − 1_t c), so ‖h − 1_t c‖₁ < δ. Finally h has compact support: support h ⊆ interior k ⊆ k with k compact (HasCompactSupport.intro: h vanishes off k). Take g := h.

4. (Closure under addition.) Let 𝒞 be the class of g : ℝ^N → E that are continuous, belong to L¹(ν) and have compact support. If g₁, g₂ ∈ 𝒞 then g₁ + g₂ ∈ 𝒞: sums of continuous maps are continuous, L¹(ν) is closed under addition, and tsupport(g₁ + g₂) ⊆ tsupport g₁ ∪ tsupport g₂ is compact (HasCompactSupport.add).

5. (Density.) Since p = 1 ≠ ∞ and f ∈ L¹(ν), MemLp.induction_dense applies with the property 𝒞: its first hypothesis is Step 3 (every indicator-constant 1_t c with t measurable and ν(t) < ∞ is within any δ ≠ 0 of an element of 𝒞), its second is Step 4. (Mathematically: simple functions in L¹(ν) are dense, MemLp.exists_simpleFunc_eLpNorm_sub_lt; a simple function in L¹(ν) is a finite sum Σ_i 1_{t_i} c_i with ν(t_i) < ∞ for c_i ≠ 0; approximating every term by Step 3 within a sufficiently small error and adding, by Step 4 and the triangle inequality for ‖·‖₁, gives an element of 𝒞 within any prescribed error of the simple function, hence of f.) It yields, for the given ε ≠ 0, some g ∈ 𝒞 with ‖f − g‖₁ = eLpNorm (f − g) 1 ν ≤ ε.

6. (Conclusion.) This g satisfies HasCompactSupport g, eLpNorm (f − g) 1 ν ≤ ε, Continuous g and MemLp g 1 ν, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Finite Borel measures on ℝ^N are outer regular and inner regular by compact (closed) sets; ‖c·1_s‖₁ = ‖c‖ν(s) is small when ν(s) is small (exists_eLpNorm_indicator_le).

Urysohn: for closed s ⊆ open u with ν(s) < ∞, take open V ⊇ s with ν(V∖s) small and φ: continuous, 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on s, φ = 0 off u ∩ V; then φ·c is continuous, supported in u, and ‖φc − 1_s c‖₁ ≤ ‖1_{(u∩V)∖s} c‖₁ is small.

For measurable t with ν(t) < ∞: compact closed s ⊆ t with ν(t∖s) small, a compact k with s ⊆ interior k, and the Urysohn function for (s, interior k) give a continuous compactly supported L¹ map within any δ of c·1_t (triangle inequality, exists_Lp_half).

Continuous compactly supported L¹ maps are closed under addition; MemLp.induction_dense (density of simple functions in L¹, p = 1 ≠ ∞) extends the approximation from indicator-constants to every f ∈ L¹(ν).

audit.reason: Finite Borel regularity, Urysohn approximation of indicators, compact neighborhoods and MemLp.induction_dense give every requested conclusion. The proof works for the stated general real normed space without completeness, and covers every nonzero ENNReal tolerance. It supplies a complete construction rather than a future proof plan.

subproblem.title: Polar approximation on a ball: ∫_B ‖g‖ dμ ≤ ∫⟨F, g⟩ dμ + ε for a continuous F with ‖F‖ ≤ 1 and tsupport F ⊆ B (Steps 3, 5, 6 of the supplied proof)
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let E be a real inner product space (E : Type with NormedAddCommGroup E and InnerProductSpace ℝ E), let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Eucl N, let R ∈ ℝ, B := ball(0, R) (the open ball), and let g : ℝ^N → E be μ-integrable on B (IntegrableOn g B μ). Then for every real ε > 0 there is F : ℝ^N → E such that F is continuous, tsupport F ⊆ B, ‖F(x)‖ ≤ 1 for every x, the function x ↦ ⟨F(x), g(x)⟩ (inner ℝ) is μ-integrable on ℝ^N, and ∫_B ‖g(x)‖ dμ(x) ≤ ∫ ⟨F(x), g(x)⟩ dμ(x) + ε.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] (μ : Measure (Eucl N)) (R : ℝ) (g : Eucl N → E), IntegrableOn g (ball (0 : Eucl N) R) μ → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ F : Eucl N → E, Continuous F ∧ tsupport F ⊆ ball (0 : Eucl N) R ∧ (∀ x, ‖F x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (F x) (g x)) μ ∧ ∫ x in ball (0 : Eucl N) R, ‖g x‖ ∂μ ≤ ∫ x, inner ℝ (F x) (g x) ∂μ + ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3, 5 and 6 of the supplied proof of imc_lintegral_coordNorm_le_mass (the finite measure ν = |κ|μ⌞B_R and the polar field u = κ/|κ|; the cut-off χ near ∂B_R and the radial retraction π; the estimate ∫χ⟨π(g₀), u⟩ dν ≥ ν(ℝ^N) − O(ε)), written for a vector field g with values in a real inner product space E (in the parent, g = c(κ) ∈ ℝ^I). Step 4 of the supplied proof (the L¹ approximation g₀) is the sibling l1_density.

Notation. B := ball(0, R) (open), B̄_r := closedBall(0, r), μ⌞B := μ.restrict B. ⟨·,·⟩ is the real inner product of E and ‖·‖ its norm. For a set S and a function φ, ∫_S φ dμ is the Bochner integral over S.

0. (Pairing with admissible fields.) Let F : ℝ^N → E be continuous with ‖F(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x and F(x) = 0 for x ∉ B. Then x ↦ ⟨F(x), g(x)⟩ is μ-integrable and ∫ ⟨F, g⟩ dμ = ∫_B ⟨F, g⟩ dμ.
 - It is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B: x ↦ (F(x), g(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable (F continuous, g a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B since g is μ⌞B-integrable; AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk), and (a, b) ↦ ⟨a, b⟩ is continuous (continuous_inner.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).
 - |⟨F(x), g(x)⟩| ≤ ‖F(x)‖‖g(x)‖ ≤ ‖g(x)‖ (Cauchy–Schwarz, norm_inner_le_norm), and ‖g‖ is μ⌞B-integrable. So ⟨F, g⟩ is μ-integrable on B (Integrable.mono').
 - ⟨F(x), g(x)⟩ = ⟨0, g(x)⟩ = 0 for x ∉ B. A function integrable on B whose support lies in B is integrable (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset), and its integral equals the integral over B (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).

1. (The case R ≤ 0.) Then B = ∅ (ball_eq_empty). F := 0 is continuous, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ B, ‖0‖ = 0 ≤ 1, ⟨0, g(x)⟩ = 0 is integrable, and ∫_∅ ‖g‖ dμ = 0 ≤ 0 + ε = ∫⟨0, g⟩ dμ + ε. From now on R > 0.

2. (Measurable modification and polar decomposition.) g is μ⌞B-integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B; choose a strongly measurable g̃ : ℝ^N → E with g = g̃ μ⌞B-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk, stronglyMeasurable_mk, ae_eq_mk). Put ρ(x) := ‖g̃(x)‖ ≥ 0 and u(x) := ρ(x)⁻¹·g̃(x), with the convention 0⁻¹ = 0 (so u(x) = 0 when g̃(x) = 0).
 - ρ is strongly measurable (norm), u is strongly measurable (the measurable real function ρ⁻¹ times the strongly measurable g̃).
 - For every x: ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1; ‖u(x)‖ = 1 if g̃(x) ≠ 0 (then ‖u(x)‖ = ρ(x)⁻¹ρ(x) = 1); and g̃(x) = ρ(x)·u(x) (both sides are 0 if g̃(x) = 0, and ρρ⁻¹g̃ = g̃ otherwise).
 - ρ = ‖g‖ μ⌞B-a.e., so ρ is μ⌞B-integrable and ∫_B ‖g‖ dμ = ∫_B ρ dμ.

3. (The finite measure ν.) Let ν := (μ⌞B).withDensity (x ↦ ofReal ρ(x)), i.e. ν(S) = ∫⁻_{S ∩ B} ofReal ρ dμ for measurable S.
 - ν(ℝ^N) = ∫⁻_B ofReal ρ dμ = ofReal(∫_B ρ dμ) < ∞ (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, ρ ≥ 0 integrable), so ν is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_withDensity).
 - For measurable S ⊆ B: ν(S) = ∫⁻_S ofReal ρ dμ = ofReal(∫_S ρ dμ) (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, S ∩ B = S, and ρ integrable on S ⊆ B).
 - u ∈ L¹(ν): u is strongly measurable, ‖u‖ ≤ 1 and ν is finite (MemLp.of_bound).

4. (Inner radius R'.) Claim: there is R' with 0 < R' < R and ν(B ∖ B̄_{R'}) < ofReal(ε/4).
 - For n ∈ ℕ let r_n := R − R/(n + 2) and s_n := B ∖ B̄_{r_n}. Since R > 0, r_n is increasing in n, so (s_n) is decreasing; each s_n is measurable (open minus closed); ν(s_0) < ∞.
 - ⋂_n s_n = ∅: if x ∈ B then ‖x‖ < R; choose n ∈ ℕ with n > R/(R − ‖x‖) (Archimedes); then R/(n + 2) < R − ‖x‖, i.e. ‖x‖ < r_n, so x ∈ B̄_{r_n} and x ∉ s_n. Points outside B lie in no s_n.
 - By continuity from above of the finite measure ν (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop), ν(s_n) → ν(∅) = 0. As ofReal(ε/4) > 0, some n has ν(s_n) < ofReal(ε/4). Take R' := r_n; then 0 < R' (because R/(n+2) < R) and R' < R (because R/(n+2) > 0).

5. (L¹ approximation, sibling l1_density.) Apply l1_density to N, E, the finite measure ν, f := u ∈ L¹(ν) and the nonzero ε' := ofReal(ε/4): there is g₀ : ℝ^N → E with compact support, continuous (and in L¹(ν)), such that eLpNorm (u − g₀) 1 ν ≤ ofReal(ε/4). Since eLpNorm (u − g₀) 1 ν = ∫⁻ ‖u − g₀‖ₑ dν (eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm; u − g₀ is strongly measurable) and, by the integral formula for a measure with a measurable density (lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul; x ↦ ofReal ρ(x) and x ↦ ‖u(x) − g₀(x)‖ₑ are measurable), ∫⁻ ‖u − g₀‖ₑ dν = ∫⁻_B ofReal(ρ(x))·‖u(x) − g₀(x)‖ₑ dμ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(ρ(x)‖g₀(x) − u(x)‖) dμ, we get
  ∫⁻_B ofReal(ρ(x)‖g₀(x) − u(x)‖) dμ(x) ≤ ofReal(ε/4).   (5.1)
 Since g₀ is continuous with compact support it is bounded: ‖g₀(x)‖ ≤ C₀ for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).

6. (Cut-off.) Let R'' := (R + R')/2, so R' < R'' < R, and χ(x) := min{1, max{0, (R'' − ‖x‖)/(R'' − R')}}.
 - χ is continuous and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
 - If ‖x‖ ≤ R' then (R'' − ‖x‖)/(R'' − R') ≥ 1, so χ(x) = 1. If ‖x‖ ≥ R'' then (R'' − ‖x‖)/(R'' − R') ≤ 0, so χ(x) = 0.
 - Hence support χ ⊆ ball(0, R''), and tsupport χ ⊆ closure(ball(0, R'')) ⊆ B̄_{R''} ⊆ B (closure_ball_subset_closedBall, closedBall_subset_ball since R'' < R).

7. (Radial retraction.) For a ∈ E let π(a) := max{1, ‖a‖}⁻¹·a. Since max{1, ‖a‖} ≥ 1 > 0 depends continuously on a, π is continuous. ‖π(a)‖ = ‖a‖/max{1, ‖a‖} ≤ 1. Claim: ‖π(a) − b‖ ≤ 2‖a − b‖ whenever ‖b‖ ≤ 1. If ‖a‖ ≤ 1 then π(a) = a and the claim is trivial. If t := ‖a‖ > 1 then π(a) − a = (1/t − 1)a has norm (1 − 1/t)t = t − 1 ≤ ‖a‖ − ‖b‖ ≤ ‖a − b‖, so ‖π(a) − b‖ ≤ ‖π(a) − a‖ + ‖a − b‖ ≤ 2‖a − b‖. (Step 0(f) of the supplied proof shows the sharper ‖π(a) − b‖ ≤ ‖a − b‖ in an inner product space: ‖a − b‖² − ‖a/t − b‖² = t² − 1 − 2(1 − 1/t)⟨a, b⟩ ≥ (t − 1)² ≥ 0; either bound suffices below, the ε-budget is chosen for the factor 2.)

8. (The competitor F.) F(x) := χ(x)·π(g₀(x)).
 - F is continuous (χ, π and g₀ are continuous).
 - tsupport F ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ B (tsupport_smul_subset_left and Step 6); in particular F(x) = 0 for x ∉ B (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
 - ‖F(x)‖ = χ(x)‖π(g₀(x))‖ ≤ 1·1 = 1.
 By Step 0, x ↦ ⟨F(x), g(x)⟩ is μ-integrable (this is the fourth conclusion) and ∫ ⟨F, g⟩ dμ = ∫_B ⟨F, g⟩ dμ = ∫_B ⟨F, g̃⟩ dμ, the last because g = g̃ μ⌞B-a.e.

9. (Pointwise estimate.) For every x ∈ ℝ^N:
  ρ(x) − ρ(x)(1 − χ(x)) − 2ρ(x)‖g₀(x) − u(x)‖ ≤ ⟨F(x), g̃(x)⟩.   (9.1)
 By Step 2, ⟨F(x), g̃(x)⟩ = ⟨χ(x)π(g₀(x)), ρ(x)u(x)⟩ = χ(x)ρ(x)⟨π(g₀(x)), u(x)⟩ (real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right).
 - If g̃(x) = 0, then ρ(x) = 0 and both sides of (9.1) are 0.
 - Otherwise ‖u(x)‖ = 1. Write ⟨π(g₀(x)), u(x)⟩ = ⟨u(x), u(x)⟩ + ⟨π(g₀(x)) − u(x), u(x)⟩ = 1 + ⟨π(g₀(x)) − u(x), u(x)⟩ ≥ 1 − ‖π(g₀(x)) − u(x)‖·‖u(x)‖ ≥ 1 − 2‖g₀(x) − u(x)‖ (Cauchy–Schwarz, abs_real_inner_le_norm, and Step 7 with b := u(x), ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1). Multiplying by χ(x)ρ(x) ≥ 0: χρ⟨π(g₀), u⟩ ≥ χρ − 2χρ‖g₀ − u‖ ≥ χρ − 2ρ‖g₀ − u‖, using 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and ρ‖g₀ − u‖ ≥ 0. Finally χρ = ρ − ρ(1 − χ).

10. (Integrability on B.) With respect to μ⌞B the following are integrable: ρ (Step 2); ρ(1 − χ), which is ρ times the continuous function 1 − χ with values in [0, 1] (Integrable.mul_bdd); ρ‖g₀ − u‖, which is ρ times the strongly measurable function ‖g₀ − u‖ bounded by C₀ + 1 (Step 5 and ‖u‖ ≤ 1); and ⟨F, g̃⟩, which is a.e. strongly measurable with |⟨F, g̃⟩| ≤ ‖F‖‖g̃‖ ≤ ρ (Integrable.mono').

11. (The two error terms.)
 (a) ∫_B ρ(1 − χ) dμ ≤ ε/4. For x ∈ B: if ‖x‖ ≤ R' then χ(x) = 1 and ρ(x)(1 − χ(x)) = 0 ≤ 1_{B∖B̄_{R'}}(x)ρ(x); if ‖x‖ > R' then x ∈ B ∖ B̄_{R'} and ρ(x)(1 − χ(x)) ≤ ρ(x) because 0 ≤ 1 − χ ≤ 1. Hence (setIntegral_mono_on, then setIntegral_indicator with B ∩ (B ∖ B̄_{R'}) = B ∖ B̄_{R'}) ∫_B ρ(1 − χ) dμ ≤ ∫_{B∖B̄_{R'}} ρ dμ. By Step 3 (S := B ∖ B̄_{R'} ⊆ B measurable) and Step 4, ofReal(∫_{B∖B̄_{R'}} ρ dμ) = ν(B ∖ B̄_{R'}) < ofReal(ε/4), hence ∫_{B∖B̄_{R'}} ρ dμ < ε/4 (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff, ε/4 > 0).
 (b) ∫_B ρ‖g₀ − u‖ dμ ≤ ε/4. By Step 10 and nonnegativity, ofReal(∫_B ρ‖g₀ − u‖ dμ) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(ρ‖g₀ − u‖) dμ (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal), which is ≤ ofReal(ε/4) by (5.1); hence ∫_B ρ‖g₀ − u‖ dμ ≤ ε/4 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff, ε/4 ≥ 0).

12. (Conclusion.) Integrating (9.1) over B with respect to μ (integral_mono; all functions are μ⌞B-integrable by Step 10; integral_sub, integral_const_mul):
  ∫_B ρ dμ − ∫_B ρ(1 − χ) dμ − 2∫_B ρ‖g₀ − u‖ dμ ≤ ∫_B ⟨F, g̃⟩ dμ.
 By Steps 2, 8 and 11: ∫_B ‖g‖ dμ = ∫_B ρ dμ ≤ ∫_B ⟨F, g̃⟩ dμ + ε/4 + 2·(ε/4) = ∫ ⟨F, g⟩ dμ + 3ε/4 ≤ ∫ ⟨F, g⟩ dμ + ε. Together with Step 8 (continuity, tsupport F ⊆ B, ‖F‖ ≤ 1, integrability) this proves the statement. ∎

subproblem.title: Polar test form for a k-vector field: ∫⁻_B |κ| dμ ≤ ∫ κ(ω) dμ + ε with ω continuous, |ω| ≤ 1, tsupport ω ⊆ B
subproblem.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Eucl N, κ : ℝ^N → Λ_k(ℝ^N) a field of k-vectors (NVector (Eucl N) k), R ∈ ℝ and B := ball(0, R). For γ ∈ SimonMultiIndex k N let κ^γ(x) := euclideanNVectorCoordinate (κ x) γ = κ(x)(dx^γ), where dx^γ := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (γ j)), and assume that every κ^γ is μ-integrable on B. Then for every real ε > 0 there is ω : ℝ^N → Λ^k(ℝ^N) (Covector (Eucl N) k) such that ω is continuous, tsupport ω ⊆ B, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1 for every x, x ↦ κ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable, and ∫⁻_B ENNReal.ofReal(√(Σ_γ κ^γ(x)²)) dμ(x) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(∫ κ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) + ε).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl N)) (κ : Eucl N → NVector (Eucl N) k) (R : ℝ), (∀ γ : SimonMultiIndex k N, IntegrableOn (fun x => euclideanNVectorCoordinate (κ x) γ) (ball (0 : Eucl N) R) μ) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ω : Eucl N → Covector (Eucl N) k, Continuous ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ ball (0 : Eucl N) R ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ Integrable (fun x => κ x (ω x)) μ ∧ ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Eucl N) R, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (∑ γ : SimonMultiIndex k N, (euclideanNVectorCoordinate (κ x) γ) ^ 2)) ∂μ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, κ x (ω x) ∂μ + ε)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 0(a), (b), (d), (e) of the supplied proof of imc_lintegral_coordNorm_le_mass (coefficient vector c(w) := (w^γ)_γ ∈ ℝ^I, |c(w)| = |w|, a♭ := Σ_γ a_γ dx^γ with (a♭)_β = a_β, |a♭| = ‖a‖ and w(a♭) = ⟨a, c(w)⟩), together with the transfer in Steps 5–6 (f := (π∘g₀)♭·χ and κ(x)(f(x)) = ⟨F(x), c(κ(x))⟩). The analytic part of Steps 3–6 is the sibling polar_field; the linear algebra is the reused siblings coord_sum_wedge (smr_ci_coord_sum_smul_wedge) and norm_coord (smr_ci_norm_eq_sqrt_sum_coord_sq).

Notation. I := SimonMultiIndex k N (a finite type) and H := EuclideanSpace ℝ I, with ‖a‖ = √(Σ_γ a_γ²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq together with ‖r‖² = |r|² = r²) and ⟨a, b⟩ = Σ_γ a_γ b_γ (PiLp.inner_apply; for real scalars ⟨r, s⟩ = r·s), where a_γ denotes the γ-th coordinate (a.ofLp γ). B := ball(0, R). dx^γ := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (γ j)); by the definition of euclideanNVectorCoordinate, κ^γ(x) = euclideanNVectorCoordinate (κ x) γ = κ(x)(dx^γ). Put h(x) := √(Σ_γ κ^γ(x)²).

1. (The coefficient field.) Define c : ℝ^N → H by c(x) := (κ^γ(x))_γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun γ ↦ κ^γ(x))). Comparing coordinates (EuclideanSpace.single γ 1 has β-coordinate 1 if β = γ and 0 otherwise), c(x) = Σ_γ κ^γ(x)·e_γ with e_γ := EuclideanSpace.single γ 1.

2. (Integrability of c on B.) Each x ↦ κ^γ(x)·e_γ is μ-integrable on B (hypothesis, Integrable.smul_const), and a finite sum of integrable functions is integrable (integrable_finsetSum). By Step 1, c is μ-integrable on B.

3. (|c| = h.) ‖c(x)‖ = √(Σ_γ |κ^γ(x)|²) = √(Σ_γ κ^γ(x)²) = h(x) for every x (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs).

4. (Sibling polar_field.) Apply polar_field with N, E := H (a real inner product space), μ, R, g := c (integrable on B by Step 2) and ε > 0. It yields F : ℝ^N → H with F continuous, tsupport F ⊆ B, ‖F(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, x ↦ ⟨F(x), c(x)⟩ μ-integrable, and
  ∫_B ‖c(x)‖ dμ ≤ ∫ ⟨F(x), c(x)⟩ dμ + ε.   (4.1)

5. (The test field ω := F♭.) Define ω(x) := Σ_{γ ∈ I} F(x)_γ · dx^γ ∈ Covector (Eucl N) k.
 (a) Continuity: x ↦ F(x)_γ is continuous (the coordinate map a ↦ a_γ is continuous, PiLp.continuous_apply, composed with F), so ω is a finite sum of continuous scalar functions times constant covectors (continuous_finsetSum, Continuous.smul).
 (b) Support: if F(x) = 0 then every F(x)_γ = 0 and ω(x) = 0. Hence support ω ⊆ support F, so tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport F ⊆ B (closure_mono).
 (c) Norm: by the sibling coord_sum_wedge (with P := N and coefficients γ ↦ F(x)_γ), euclideanCovectorCoordinate (ω(x)) β = F(x)_β for every β ∈ I. By the sibling norm_coord, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω(x)) = √(Σ_β (euclideanCovectorCoordinate (ω(x)) β)²) = √(Σ_β F(x)_β²) = ‖F(x)‖ ≤ 1.
 (d) Pairing: κ(x) is a continuous linear functional on Covector (Eucl N) k, so κ(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_γ F(x)_γ·κ(x)(dx^γ) = Σ_γ F(x)_γ·κ^γ(x) = ⟨F(x), c(x)⟩ (map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, PiLp.inner_apply).

6. (Integrability.) By 5(d) the function x ↦ κ(x)(ω(x)) coincides with x ↦ ⟨F(x), c(x)⟩, which is μ-integrable by Step 4. Also ∫ κ(x)(ω(x)) dμ = ∫ ⟨F(x), c(x)⟩ dμ.

7. (The lower integral.) By Step 3, ∫⁻_B ofReal(h) dμ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(‖c‖) dμ. Since ‖c‖ is μ-integrable on B (Step 2) and nonnegative, ∫⁻_B ofReal(‖c‖) dμ = ofReal(∫_B ‖c‖ dμ) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). By (4.1), monotonicity of ENNReal.ofReal and Step 6: ofReal(∫_B ‖c‖ dμ) ≤ ofReal(∫ ⟨F, c⟩ dμ + ε) = ofReal(∫ κ(x)(ω(x)) dμ + ε).

8. (Conclusion.) ω is continuous (5a), tsupport ω ⊆ B (5b), covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1 (5c), x ↦ κ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable (6), and ∫⁻_B ofReal(√(Σ_γ κ^γ(x)²)) dμ ≤ ofReal(∫ κ(x)(ω(x)) dμ + ε) (7). ∎
